## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP; a Proxy row says whether a proxy variable applies, the checks themselves stay direct, DEVDESK-582) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only) + a path trace under Diagnostics (Trace Path button, or `H` on the route row; no separate tab since DEVDESK-471) (native path trace, on native Linux, native Windows (IPv4 only, ICMP echoes through `iphlpapi`, DEVDESK-486) and WSL2: on macOS and WSL1 the button, `H`, `enter` and `ctrl+o` are greyed and the footer says why, DEVDESK-334; the column starts with this machine, its interface and its gateway; `ctrl+o` can start it from a running Docker Engine container instead (container and network rows, hops still traced from this machine); `H` on the Diagnostics route row opens the trace level on that host without starting it (greyed with the reason on an unsupported platform or a target the trace refuses; its interface and gateway rows reuse the Local route check's reading of the same address, read once, DEVDESK-473), and in the trace level `enter` starts or restarts it, `ctrl+o` picks the source, `esc` cancels then goes back where it came from; under WSL2 the source row says `WSL2 (VM), not the Windows host` with the networking mode, and in NAT mode the gateway and TTL 1 hop are tagged `Windows host (virtual switch)` only when proven, DEVDESK-333; the interface row says `no route` when the kernel proves there is none and `undetermined` when the routing table could not be read, a no-route error keeps the local rows, a trace that ends on the hop limit or the deadline folds its silent tail into one `silent` row and marks the `last to answer` hop, and the target refuses a `:port`, DEVDESK-335)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line) shown as a status dot in the first column (the `running` dot blinks, DEVDESK-151) and as text, tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost` (orange from 75 % and red from 90 % of the session's estimated cost, when at least two agents are priced), from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, when its transcript is gone, or while the terminal is not focused (header `Updates › paused`, then `paused (terminal not focused)`; `app.when_unfocused: run` keeps it live); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go
mise run ci           # the five checks in order (fmt-check, vet, lint, build, test-race), stops at the first failure; unlike check it rewrites no file and also runs build and test-race. `test-race` is the only test run (`-race` covers `go test`); `mise run test` stays available alone for the fast local loop. CI runs fmt-check, vet, lint and build in the `Lint and build` job and `test-race` in the `Test` job, on every pull request, docs-only ones included (the docs-only shortcut applies to `Lint and build` only); the whole CI targets under 10 minutes, so run this locally before a PR to catch a red check early

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

**Nexus tests replay recorded fixtures (DEVDESK-511, DEVDESK-580).** Three campaigns
in `internal/nexusfixture/fixtures/` (`catalog`, `cachedonly`, `access`) replay through
`fakenexus`: `mise run test` needs no bench, cluster or secret. A `record: pending` file is never
versioned (`TestNoPendingFixtureIsVersioned`); `DEVDESK_FIXTURE_RECORDING=1` only in a local recording session.
`nexus-bench record` without `--state` applies no state filter and can overwrite an `upstream-cut` fixture.
Bench writes go only through `nexus-bench:*` tasks and the guarded `DEVDESK_NEXUS_BENCH_SCENARIOS=1` test.
Dated measures live in `docs/measurements/`; a measure contradicting a criterion or the code is frozen and noted, never fixed in the same PR.

**Scanner containers and the proxy (DEVDESK-583, D164).** Every `run --rm` a scanner
issues goes through `containerRun{…}.cmd()` (`internal/scan/container_run.go`): the proxy
variables travel as `-e NAME` with the value in the child environment, never in argv. The
guard `TestContainerGuard*` (`internal/netproxy/container_guard_test.go`) fails on any other
`"run"` literal; only the two permanent exceptions in that file are allowed. The tests of
`internal/scan`, `internal/app` and `internal/ui/security` neutralise the seams
`proxyForward` / `containerForward` in their `TestMain`, so a developer's `HTTPS_PROXY` does not
change an exact argv. The `TestMain` of `internal/app`
also replaces `detectTools` (`internal/app/scan_tools.go`, production value `scan.Detect`) with an
empty report, so `App.Init` never runs the `trivy`, `gitleaks` and `plumber` of the machine
(DEVDESK-645); `TestInitDoesNotRunTheScannersOfTheHost` and `TestDetectToolsIsScanDetectInProduction`
guard it.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. **Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

**Nexus tests replay recorded fixtures (DEVDESK-511, DEVDESK-580).** Three campaigns
in `internal/nexusfixture/fixtures/` (`catalog`, `cachedonly`, `access`) replay through
`fakenexus`: `mise run test` needs no bench, cluster or secret. A `record: pending` file is never
versioned (`TestNoPendingFixtureIsVersioned`); `DEVDESK_FIXTURE_RECORDING=1` only in a local recording session.
`nexus-bench record` without `--state` applies no state filter and can overwrite an `upstream-cut` fixture.
Bench writes go only through `nexus-bench:*` tasks and the guarded `DEVDESK_NEXUS_BENCH_SCENARIOS=1` test.
Dated measures live in `docs/measurements/`; a measure contradicting a criterion or the code is frozen and noted, never fixed in the same PR.

**Scanner containers and the proxy (DEVDESK-583, D164).** Every `run --rm` a scanner
issues goes through `containerRun{…}.cmd()` (`internal/scan/container_run.go`): the proxy
variables travel as `-e NAME` with the value in the child environment, never in argv. The
guard `TestContainerGuard*` (`internal/netproxy/container_guard_test.go`) fails on any other
`"run"` literal; only the two permanent exceptions in that file are allowed. The tests of
`internal/scan`, `internal/app` and `internal/ui/security` neutralise the seams
`proxyForward` / `containerForward` in their `TestMain`, so a developer's `HTTPS_PROXY` does not
change an exact argv. The `TestMain` of `internal/app`
also replaces `detectTools` (`internal/app/scan_tools.go`, production value `scan.Detect`) with an
empty report, so `App.Init` never runs the `trivy`, `gitleaks` and `plumber` of the machine
(DEVDESK-645); `TestInitDoesNotRunTheScannersOfTheHost` and `TestDetectToolsIsScanDetectInProduction`
guard it.

**Tests and the host secret store (DEVDESK-610).** By default `credentials.Select` and
`KeyringAvailable` reach the real keyring of the machine (Secret Service over D-Bus on
Linux); a locked keyring blocks the whole suite until the timeout. A test binary that can
reach them isolates the store: `fakekeyring.Install()` in `TestMain`, then
`fakekeyring.Fresh(t)` (or `FreshUnreachable(t, err)` for a locked keyring) per test, from
`internal/testutil/fakekeyring`. `isolateHome(t)` already calls `Fresh` in `internal/app` and
`internal/ui/setup`. Two guards enforce it: at run time, any keyring or `git credential` call
in a test binary without the fake panics with `DEVDESK-610` and the operation; statically,
`TestHostStoreGuard*` (`internal/credentials/hoststore_guard_test.go`) fails on K1 (go-keyring
imported outside `internal/credentials`), K2 (`SwapHostStoreForTest` in non-test code) and K3
(`fakekeyring` imported by non-test code). The seam is `credentials.HostStore` and
`SwapHostStoreForTest`, reserved for tests (it panics outside a test binary). Limits: the
runtime guard only sees the paths a test runs; the static one misses an aliased package
name, a dynamic import and an external binary; `gitHelperUsable` reads the git config
unguarded; `Install` and `Fresh` are global, so no `t.Parallel`. See
`docs/architecture/configuration.md`, "Testing code that reaches the secret store".

**Test input and colour (DEVDESK-199).** Build keys only through
`internal/ui/testutil` (`Key`, `Keys`, `Type`, `Paste`, `Text`, `IsText`), never a
literal `tea.KeyPressMsg` or `tea.Key*`. `Key` returns a
`tea.KeyPressMsg` (`Keys` and `Type` return a message list), `Paste` a `tea.PasteMsg`; `Key` is strict: an unknown name
panics. The space key is built as a key (`Key("space")`), never matched through
`String()` (v1 `" "`, v2 `"space"`). Lip Gloss v2 has no global colour profile (`Style.Render` always emits full
colour), so a test needs no setup to check styling; it reads the SGR or strips it
with `ansi.Strip`. `internal/ui/testutil/source_guard_test.go` fails the suite on a
hand-built key, a `colorprofile` import outside `internal/app/profile_test.go` and
`internal/app/redraw_measure_test.go` or `SetColorProfile` in any `_test.go`. Paste tests
(`internal/app/paste_test.go`, `wrapped_input_test.go`, `component_form_test.go`):
a paste reaches the focused field, newlines become spaces in single-line fields,
and no key action fires (Rule 111).

**Space and key API (DEVDESK-200).** Production code matches the space key as
`keymap.Space`, never `" "`/`"space"`, and reads keys through `String()` only
(no `.Runes`, `.Alt`, `.Paste`, `tea.KeyType` or `tea.Key<Name>`). Update
handlers switch on `tea.KeyPressMsg`, never the `tea.KeyMsg` interface (it also
matches releases). A paste is a `tea.PasteMsg`, not a key (Rule 111). Guards in
`internal/ui/keymap` (`space_scan_test.go`, `legacy_key_scan_test.go`,
`viewport_keymap_scan_test.go`) fail the suite otherwise; limits are listed in
`docs/architecture/app-shell.md`.

## Code Conventions

- Comments: **English only** (Rule 307) — existing French comments are not rewritten wholesale, but any new or edited comment is in English
- Commit messages: **English only** (Rule 307)
- UI text and logs: **English US only** (Rule 129)
- Bubbletea models define their own message types
- Use `theme` package for consistent styling (`internal/ui/theme/`)
- Config changes must call `config.Save()` to persist
- All colors defined in `theme/colors.go`, all styles in `theme/styles.go`
- Message naming: `[ComponentName][Action]Msg` (e.g., `ComponentFormSubmitMsg`)
- Context names: the rule exists twice (`config.ValidateContextName`, `contextcmd.ValidName`); change both or neither (`TestContextNameRulesAgree`). Creation refuses `-`, `new`, `list` (`config.ValidateNewContextName`); loading does not (D91)

## Critical Bubble Tea Rules

**NEVER modify model state inside a Cmd** (Rule 110) - Race condition:
- `Update()` is the ONLY place to modify model state
- `View()` is read-only
- `Cmd` functions do I/O and return messages

**NEVER use `style.Render()` inside `table.Row{}`** (Rule 122) - ANSI sequences corrupt all subsequent rows:
- Use plain text: `theme.IconError + " error"` not `theme.StatusErrorStyle.Render(...)`
- Apply row styling via `table.SetStyles(theme.TableStylesForState("error"))`

**Views render through `Render()`** (Bubble Tea v2): a top-level view implements
`Render() string` and `View() tea.View { return tea.NewView(m.Render()) }`; only the
router (`App.View()`) sets terminal state such as `AltScreen` and `BackgroundColor`. Components keep
`View() string`. Colours are `color.Color`; hex literals stay in `theme/colors.go`.

**Update() case extraction**: If a case block exceeds 5 lines, extract to `handle[MessageType]()` method returning `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

## Critical rules (summary)

**Rule 110** — NEVER modify the model inside a `Cmd` → race condition. Only `Update()` modifies the model.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer, never in the body: with the shared activity dot (`Status.Activity`, `●`/`○`, `SetBlinkPhase`), for a view's own load as well as for work the router tracks. The braille spinner API is removed (DEVDESK-377): nothing under `internal/` imports `bubbles/v2/spinner` or names `Status.Spinner`, `SetSpinnerFrame`, `theme.SpinnerMessage` or `theme.SpinnerStyle` (`TestNoViewImportsTheBubblesSpinner`, `TestRemovedSpinnerSymbolsStayGone`), with no exception. A new `Activity` value not driven by the jobs registry must implement `WantsBlink()`, or the dot stays fixed.

**Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a loading screen or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.

**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.

**Rule 140** — An invalid form field is underlined through `theme.StyleInvalidField` (the only entry point to the underline API), and the error is also in the footer at level Error, derived on every render. The underline is never the only carrier.

**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

The per-topic TUI rule files above load when a matching file is read or edited; when reviewing a diff without opening files, read them explicitly.

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)

mise run dev          # Run directly with go run

mise run run          # Build and run

mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

**Nexus tests replay recorded fixtures (DEVDESK-511, DEVDESK-580).** Three campaigns
in `internal/nexusfixture/fixtures/` (`catalog`, `cachedonly`, `access`) replay through
`fakenexus`: `mise run test` needs no bench, cluster or secret. A `record: pending` file is never
versioned (`TestNoPendingFixtureIsVersioned`); `DEVDESK_FIXTURE_RECORDING=1` only in a local recording session.
`nexus-bench record` without `--state` applies no state filter and can overwrite an `upstream-cut` fixture.
Bench writes go only through `nexus-bench:*` tasks and the guarded `DEVDESK_NEXUS_BENCH_SCENARIOS=1` test.
Dated measures live in `docs/measurements/`; a measure contradicting a criterion or the code is frozen and noted, never fixed in the same PR.

**Scanner containers and the proxy (DEVDESK-583, D164).** Every `run --rm` a scanner
issues goes through `containerRun{…}.cmd()` (`internal/scan/container_run.go`): the proxy
variables travel as `-e NAME` with the value in the child environment, never in argv. The
guard `TestContainerGuard*` (`internal/netproxy/container_guard_test.go`) fails on any other
`"run"` literal; only the two permanent exceptions in that file are allowed. The tests of
`internal/scan`, `internal/app` and `internal/ui/security` neutralise the seams
`proxyForward` / `containerForward` in their `TestMain`, so a developer's `HTTPS_PROXY` does not
change an exact argv. The `TestMain` of `internal/app`
also replaces `detectTools` (`internal/app/scan_tools.go`, production value `scan.Detect`) with an
empty report, so `App.Init` never runs the `trivy`, `gitleaks` and `plumber` of the machine

runtime guard only sees the paths a test runs; the static one misses an aliased package
name, a dynamic import and an external binary; `gitHelperUsable` reads the git config
unguarded; `Install` and `Fresh` are global, so no `t.Parallel`. See
`docs/architecture/configuration.md`, "Testing code that reaches the secret store".

7

9

11	
12	§3.80 a écarté Kyverno pour ne pas multiplier les outils : `kyverno apply` n'embarque aucune politique, ce n'est donc pas un catalogue de plus. 13

15	
16	- Source des politiques : **un répertoire local** (réglage envisagé `scan.kyverno_policies`). L'étage ne tourne que s'il est renseigné. Pas de dépôt git ni d'URL dans ce jalon.
17	- Affichage : les violations sont des findings de la catégorie **Misconfiguration**, onglet Misconfigurations existant, colonne Source `kyverno` (même décision que pour kubeconform, §3.80).

20	- Les règles `mutate` ne servent pas de correctif (elles réécrivent la ressource entière, réserve de §3.78).

23	
24	- Un rapport Kyverno (`--policy-report --output-format json`) donne-t-il un numéro de ligne ? Sinon, comment le retrouver (pointeur de ressource → ligne, comme `internal/k8s` le fait pour kubeconform) ?
25	- Le mode d'exécution de l'outil (`auto | binary | image`) et son entrée dans la table des outils (`internal/scan/toolbox.go`, §3.86) : quelle catégorie, quelle dépendance, quel signalement s'il est absent.
26	- Comportement sur politique invalide, aucun manifeste, politique de type `generate` ou `verifyImages`.
27

29	
30	- Pas de téléchargement de politiques (git, URL), pas de catalogue livré avec DevDesk.
31	- Pas de correctif automatique à partir de `mutate`.
32	- Pas de contrôles croisés entre objets ni de sondes liveness/readiness (DEVDESK-11).

16522	
16523	**Plane:** DEVDESK-10, DEVDESK-11
16524	
16525	§3.80 a écarté Kyverno et kube-linter pour ne pas multiplier les outils. Deux
16526	besoins restent, et ils ne se ressemblent pas.
16527	
16528	**Kyverno comme *policy-as-code* de l'utilisateur.** `kyverno apply` (1.19.1,
16529	vérifié dans `cmd/cli/kubectl-kyverno/commands/apply/command.go`) n'embarque
16530	**aucune** politique : il lui faut un chemin, une URL ou un dépôt git. Sa
16531	valeur n'est donc pas un catalogue de plus, c'est de faire respecter **les
16532	règles d'une organisation** — ce que ni Trivy ni kubeconform ne savent faire.
16533	La forme naturelle serait un réglage `scan.kyverno_policies` (un répertoire),
16534	l'étage ne tournant que s'il est renseigné ; `--policy-report --output-format
16535	json` donne un rapport lisible. Kyverno ne rendant ni Helm ni Kustomize, il
16536	lirait ce que l'étage `k8s-schema` rend déjà — le rendu serait à partager
16537	plutôt qu'à refaire. Ses règles `mutate` réécrivent la ressource entière : la
16538	réserve de §3.78 tient, elles ne serviraient pas de correctif.
16539	
16540	**Ce que seul kube-linter aurait vu.** Les sondes liveness/readiness absentes,
16541	et les contrôles **croisés** entre objets — un Service dont le sélecteur ne
16542	correspond à aucun Deployment, un ServiceAccount référencé qui n'existe pas.
16543	Ni Trivy ni kubeconform ne raisonnent sur plusieurs objets à la fois. Si le
16544	besoin se confirme, la question sera de nouveau celle de §3.80 : un outil de
16545	plus, sans numéro de ligne, ou une poignée de contrôles écrits ici sur ce que
16546	`k8s.Discover` et le rendu produisent déjà.
16547	
16548	### 3.86 Scanners — catégories, outils, onglet Tools — **done**
16549	
16550	Plan : [`2026-09-22-scanner-tools.md`](../.claude/plans/2026-09-22-scanner-tools.md),
16551	quatre PR. L'utilisateur choisissait des **catégories** (six cases), jamais des
16552	**outils** : le lien catégorie → outil était écrit en dur à chaque endroit qui
16553	en avait besoin, et chaque copie répondait à une question un peu différente.
16554	Plumber absent n'était jamais signalé par un scan ; helm et kustomize étaient
16555	signalés manquants par le dashboard alors qu'aucun réglage ne les demandait.
16556	
16557	#### PR 1 — le modèle — **done**
16558	
16559	- **Deux tables, une seule vérité** (`internal/scan/toolbox.go`) : les outils
16560	  (`Tool`) et les catégories (`ToolCategory` → `CategoryTool{Tool, Role,
16561	  DependsOn, Targets, Server, Default}`). `Uses(cat, tool)` — catégorie
16562	  activée, outil coché, dépendance cochée — est lue par chaque garde d'étage,
16563	  par `missingToolErrors` et par `Report.Missing` ; `Required` en dérive.
16564	  kubeconform est un outil de Misconfiguration (ses findings y étaient déjà
16565	  rangés par `Categorize`), helm et kustomize en dépendent.
16566	- **`Detect(tools) Report`** remplace `CheckDependencies` et les 30 champs de
16567	  `DependencyStatus` : une boucle sur la table, `Report.Status/Spec/Available`,
16568	  `Missing`, `CanScan(target)`. Un outil absent de la table n'existe nulle part —
16569	  c'est ce qui a manqué à plumber dans `toolConfig()` jusqu'à §3.80.
16570	- **Schéma `scan.categories` + `scan.tools`**, migré par `migrateScanSection`
16571	  (voir `docs/architecture/configuration.md`). `config` déclare les
16572	  identifiants et les cases cochées par défaut, faute de pouvoir importer
16573	  `scan` ; `TestTheTablesAndTheConfigurationAgree` tient les deux ensemble.
16574	- **Plumber est signalé** comme les autres quand CI est activé. Les renderers
16575	  ne le sont pas dans `Result.Errors` : sans eux l'étage tourne quand même et
16576	  nomme chaque chart non rendu (`K8sUnrendered`), plus précis qu'une ligne par
16577	  scan.
16578	- **Interface inchangée en apparence.** L'onglet `scan` garde ses six cases ;
16579	  « Misconfiguration » et « K8s schema » sont deux groupes d'outils de la même
16580	  catégorie (`toolToggle`, `setToolGroup`) qui se comportent comme les deux
16581	  interrupteurs indépendants qu'ils étaient. Le serveur Trivy ne décoche plus
16582	  que **la part de Trivy** dans Misconfiguration : la validation de schéma
16583	  reste (constat 5 du plan, réglé en passant puisque c'était gratuit).
16584	- `TestEveryConfiguredOptionReachesTheScanner` descend désormais jusqu'aux
16585	  réglages de chaque outil ; `TestNewScannerHonoursEveryToolsSource` parcourt
16586	  la table — un outil ajouté y est couvert sans être nommé.
16587

16590	`CanScan(categories, target)` prennent les catégories. Ainsi une case cochée
16591	change le verdict sans nouvelle détection, ce que la PR 2 exige.

16593	#### PR 2 — détection partagée, dashboard, disponibilité — **done**
16594	
16595	- **Une seule détection**, tenue par le routeur (`internal/app/scan_tools.go`)
16596	  dans `shared.State.Tools *scan.Report` et diffusée à chaque vue

15502	### 3.80 Manifestes Kubernetes — analyser et corriger, sans jamais toucher un cluster — **done**
15503	
15504	Kubernetes entre dans le périmètre de DevDesk du côté **fichier**, pas du côté
15505	exécution : lire des manifestes, YAML ou Helm, dans un dépôt ou un
15506	workspace, et faire pour eux ce que §3.2 et §3.78 font déjà pour les
15507	Dockerfiles — détecter, et corriger ce qui se corrige de façon sûre. Pas de
15508	connexion à un cluster, pas de `kubectl`, pas de pod qui tourne : DevDesk

15510	
15511	Lu pour cette entrée : *Docker and Kubernetes Security* (2025), chapitre 6
15512	(« Securing Containers in Kubernetes ») et §3.6.4 (Kubescape), un Docker
15513	Captain comme auteur.
15514	
15515	**Premier fait vérifié, pas supposé : DevDesk détecte déjà des
15516	misconfigurations Kubernetes, aujourd'hui, sans rien changer.**
15517	
15518	```
15519	$ trivy fs --scanners misconfig ./repo-avec-un-deployment.yaml
15520	Type: kubernetes, ID: KSV-0001  "Can elevate its own privileges"
15521	Type: kubernetes, ID: KSV-0012  "Runs as root user"
15522	Type: kubernetes, ID: KSV-0013  Image tag ":latest" used
15523	…
15524	```
15525	
15526	`trivyMisconfigArgs` (`internal/scan/trivy_args.go:169`) lance déjà `trivy fs
15527	--scanners misconfig` sur tout workspace scanné — la même commande qui trouve
15528	les problèmes de Dockerfile trouve, sans le savoir, les manifestes Kubernetes
15529	qu'un dépôt contient. Vérifié en local (Trivy 0.71.2) sur un `Deployment` avec
15530	`privileged: true` : six `KSV-*` remontent, avec span, sévérité et
15531	`Resolution`, exactement le même format que les `DS*`/`AVD-DS-*` déjà utilisés
15532	par le catalogue §3.78.
15533	
15534	**Ce qui manque n'est donc pas la détection — c'est de savoir de quel dialecte
15535	IaC vient un finding.** `TrivyResult.Type` (`internal/scan/trivy.go:20`, valeur
15536	`"kubernetes"`, `"dockerfile"`, `"terraform"`, `"cloudformation"`, `"helm"`…)
15537	est décodé et **jeté** : `scan.Finding` n'a aucun champ qui le porte. C'est
15538	exactement la forme du trou que la phase A de §3.78 a refermé pour
15539	`EndLine`/`Message`/`Status` — un champ que Trivy rend déjà et que la
15540	construction du `Finding` ne garde pas. Sans lui, impossible de grouper les
15541	findings par manifeste, de leur donner un libellé distinct dans l'onglet
15542	Misconfigurations, ou d'indexer un catalogue de correctifs par dialecte.
15543	
15544	Le texte de la décision B2 de §3.78 l'anticipait déjà sans le construire :
15545	*« … sinon la colonne proposerait d'écrire un Dockerfile sur un onglet qui
15546	liste aussi des manifestes Kubernetes »* (§3.78, table des décisions, ligne
15547	1) — l'onglet existant a été conçu en sachant que ce jour viendrait.
15548	
15549	**Le piège que §3.78 a déjà noté, et qu'il faut prendre au sérieux ici** :
15550	*« YAML, Kubernetes et Terraform sont la classe la plus nombreuse et celle où
15551	`Rewrite` par span ne suffit plus : la correction y est souvent ajouter une
15552	clé dans un mapping, ce qui demande un parseur préservant indentation et
15553	commentaires. »* Concrètement :
15554

## Code quality rules and proactive checks

### Rule 301 : Systematic code quality check before commit

**MANDATORY**: Before creating a commit, ALWAYS perform the following checks:

#### 1. Go linter (golangci-lint)
```bash
golangci-lint run
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Fix ALL warnings and errors
- ✅ Specifically check deprecation warnings (SA1019)
- ✅ NEVER ignore warnings without documented justification

#### 2. Tests
```bash
go test ./...
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Verify that all tests pass
- ✅ If tests fail, fix them BEFORE the commit

#### 3. Build
```bash
go build
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Verify that the build succeeds without errors
- ✅ Test the application if functional changes were made

#### 4. Deprecated dependencies

**Detection:**
- Check golangci-lint SA1019 warnings
- Look in go.mod for packages marked as deprecated

**Action:**
- Replace IMMEDIATELY with a maintained alternative
- Document the replacement in the commit message
- Update the documentation (.claude/CLAUDE.md)

**Examples of common replacements:**
- `github.com/go-ping/ping` → `github.com/prometheus-community/pro-bing`

### Rule 302 : IDE diagnostics check

**MANDATORY**: Before each commit, check the IDE diagnostics:

```
Use mcp__ide__getDiagnostics to check:
- Compilation errors
- Unused parameters
- Unused imports
- Other warnings
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Fix or justify every diagnostic
- ✅ Do not ignore "unused parameter" without a reason

### Rule 303 : go.mod and dependencies

**After any dependency change:**

```bash
go mod tidy
go mod verify
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Verify that go.mod is up to date
- ✅ Verify that go.sum is consistent
- ✅ Document new dependencies in .claude/CLAUDE.md

### Rule 304 : Quality commit message

**Mandatory format for quality fixes — in English (see Rule 307):**

```
type: short description

Detailed description explaining:
- What was detected (warning, error, etc.)
- Why it was a problem
- How it was resolved

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
```

**Commit types for quality:**
- `fix:` - Bug fix detected by linter
- `chore:` - Deprecated dependency replacement
- `refactor:` - Code quality improvement

### Rule 305 : MANDATORY pre-commit checklist

**Before EVERY commit, check:**

- [ ] `golangci-lint run` → 0 warnings
- [ ] `go test ./...` → PASS
- [ ] `go build` → SUCCESS
- [ ] `mcp__ide__getDiagnostics` → No critical error
- [ ] `go.mod` up to date (if dependencies changed)
- [ ] Documentation updated (if API changed)
- [ ] Tests added (if new feature)

**If EVEN ONE of these checks fails:**
- ❌ DO NOT create the commit
- ✅ Fix it first
- ✅ Restart the checklist

### Rule 306 : MANDATORY proactivity

**Claude Code MUST:**
- ✅ Check the linter WITHOUT the user asking
- ✅ Propose fixes BEFORE the commit
- ✅ Flag deprecated dependencies AS SOON AS they are detected
- ✅ Document all quality changes

**Claude Code MUST NEVER:**
- ❌ Wait for the user to flag a warning
- ❌ Create a commit with unresolved warnings
- ❌ Ignore dependency issues
- ❌ Forget to update the documentation

### Correct workflow examples

**Example 1 - Feature commit:**
```
1. Write the code
2. go build → verify compilation
3. golangci-lint run → fix warnings
4. go test ./... → verify tests
5. mcp__ide__getDiagnostics → check the IDE
6. git commit with a detailed message
```

**Example 2 - Detecting a deprecated dependency:**
```
1. golangci-lint detects SA1019
2. Look up the recommended alternative
3. Replace the import and the code
4. go mod tidy
5. Test that everything works
6. Update .claude/CLAUDE.md
7. git commit explaining the replacement
```

### Rule 307 : Commits and code comments — English only

**Every git commit message and every comment in the code must be written
in English**, regardless of the language used to converse with the user.

| Element | Language |
|---------|--------|
| Commit message (title + body) | ✅ English only |
| Code comment (`//`, `/* */`, docstring) | ✅ English only |
| Replies to the user in the conversation | The user's language (see memory `feedback-langue-francais`) |
| UI and logs (Rule 129) | English US only — already covered, unchanged |

This **replaces** the earlier tolerance listed in `.claude/CLAUDE.md` under
"Code Conventions" ("Comments: French or English both accepted"): existing
French comments are not to be rewritten wholesale, but any new comment and
any edit to an existing comment must be in English.

```
// ✅ CORRECT
// retry with backoff because the API rate-limits bursts above 10 req/s

// ❌ WRONG (a French comment, which Rule 307 forbids)
// on relance avec un backoff car l'API limite les rafales au-delà de 10 req/s
```

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Contre-expertise de DEVDESK-10 (Kyverno appliqué aux manifestes d'un dépôt scanné). J'ai lu `docs/product/kyverno-policies/brief.md`, les §3.80, §3.85 et §3.86 de `docs/backlog.md`, `internal/scan/toolbox.go` (lignes 140-247) et `internal/k8s/discover.go`. Je n'ai rien exécuté : aucun `kyverno apply` n'a tourné, et les comportements de la CLI cités viennent de sa documentation, pas d'une mesure.

## Failles, de la plus grave à la moins grave

**1. Le rapport Kyverno ne pointe ni un fichier ni une ligne, et le passage d'une ressource à un fichier peut être ambigu.**
- **Pourquoi c'est un risque.** Le rapport de politiques désigne une ressource par (kind, namespace, name), sans chemin de fichier. Or §3.80 a écarté kube-linter précisément parce qu'il ne rendait pas de numéro de ligne. Le pointeur JSON → ligne de `internal/k8s` (`yamlpath.go`) suppose de connaître le fichier de départ.
- **Ce qui rend la correspondance ambiguë :**
  - le même `Deployment/app` apparaît dans `base/` et dans chaque overlay ;
  - beaucoup de manifestes n'ont pas de `metadata.namespace` (il est fixé au déploiement par `kubectl -n` ou par Kustomize) ;
  - au jalon 2, une ressource rendue par Helm n'a aucune ligne dans un fichier source.
- **Conséquence.** Sans ligne, le finding perd le saut à la ligne et toute mesure de la correction par re-scan. C'est un finding de moindre qualité que ceux de Trivy et de kubeconform sur le même onglet.
- **Vérification.** Un `kyverno apply -p --output-format json` sur un dépôt réel qui a une base et deux overlays. Compter les violations rattachables à un seul fichier et une seule ligne.

**2. Des politiques réelles supposent un cluster ou une requête d'admission. Hors cluster, elles échouent, sont sautées ou passent sans rien vérifier.**
- **Ce qui manque hors cluster :**
  - le contexte : `apiCall`, `configMap`, `imageRegistry` ;
  - les variables d'admission : `request.operation`, `request.userInfo`, `request.namespace`, `serviceAccountName` ;
  - les sélecteurs de namespace (`namespaceSelector`), qui lisent les labels du namespace dans le cluster ;
  - les exclusions par rôle et les règles posées avec `background: false`.
- **Ce que la CLI propose.** `--values-file` et `--context-file` (le second pour les politiques CEL), ou `--cluster`, qui est exclu par le non-objectif « pas de client de cluster ». La documentation ne dit pas ce que fait un `apiCall` sans cluster.
- **Conséquence.** Faux négatifs silencieux, ou des erreurs qui noient les vraies violations. Le brief ne prévoit aucun moyen de fournir ces valeurs.
- **Vérification.** Récupérer le vrai jeu de politiques de l'organisation et compter celles qui utilisent un `context` ou `request.*` ou un `namespaceSelector`. Puis lancer `apply` hors cluster et classer le résultat de chaque politique en pass, fail, skip ou error.

**3. Le gain sur l'existant n'est pas démontré : l'organisation fait probablement déjà respecter ces règles ailleurs.**
- **Pourquoi c'est un risque.** Une organisation qui maintient des politiques Kyverno a presque toujours le contrôleur d'admission sur ses clusters, souvent aussi `kyverno apply` ou `kyverno test` en CI. DevDesk ne ferait que rapprocher ce retour du poste du développeur.
- **Alternatives « assez bonnes » :**
  - une ligne `kyverno apply` dans le pipeline ;
  - un hook pre-commit ;
  - les checks personnalisés de Trivy, qui est déjà intégré (`--config-check`, en Rego) et qui couvrent les mêmes règles d'organisation (étiquettes obligatoires, registres autorisés) sans outil de plus.
- **Hypothèse cachée.** Le brief suppose que l'utilisateur a un répertoire local de politiques. En pratique, ces politiques vivent dans un dépôt plateform, ou seulement dans le cluster. Exclure git et les URL vide peut-être le jalon 1 de ses utilisateurs.
- **Vérification.** Deux ou trois entretiens : où vivent vos politiques ? Sont-elles déjà en CI ou en admission ? Combien de fois un refus à l'admission vous a-t-il surpris ?

**4. La cohérence avec §3.80 et §3.86 est fragile, et la gravité fixée par défaut fausse le tri.**
- **Un outil de plus, d'un genre nouveau.** C'est un 8e outil, alors que §3.80 demande « ne pas multiplier les outils, les traiter tous de la même manière ». La table `categoryTable` (`internal/scan/toolbox.go`, ligne 192) relie un outil à des cases à cocher. Ici, l'étage dépend d'un réglage de chemin, pas d'une case. `Uses`, `Required` et `Missing` ne savent pas exprimer « requis seulement si `scan.kyverno_policies` est renseigné ». Il faut décider si kyverno est signalé manquant quand le chemin est vide ou invalide. La question rejoint celle de helm et kustomize, que §3.86 a révisée.
- **La gravité par défaut.** L'annotation `policies.kyverno.io/severity` est facultative, et les politiques maison l'omettent souvent. Tout tombe alors en Medium, mêlé aux règles `KSV-*` de Trivy. De plus, `validationFailureAction` (Audit ou Enforce) est ignoré : une règle qui bloque réellement le déploiement apparaît au même niveau qu'une simple recommandation.
- **Les doublons.** Une politique sur le tag `:latest` ou sur `privileged` recouvre une règle `KSV-*` et produit un doublon non dédupliqué sur le même onglet.
- **Vérification.**
  - Dans le jeu de politiques réel, compter les politiques annotées et la répartition Audit / Enforce.
  - Lister les recouvrements avec les `KSV-*` remontés par Trivy.
  - Esquisser la ligne kyverno dans `categoryTable` et vérifier que `TestTheTablesAndTheConfigurationAgree` tient sans cas spécial.

**5. Le jalon 1 (manifestes bruts seulement) risque de ne rien prouver, et le jalon 2 peut contredire le jalon 1.**
- **Pourquoi c'est un risque.** Dans les dépôts visés, les manifestes sont surtout des charts Helm ou des bases Kustomize. Une base n'est pas ce qui est déployé : l'overlay ajoute les labels, le namespace, les limites, le registre. Le jalon 1 produit donc des faux positifs (« label obligatoire absent » alors qu'un `commonLabels` l'ajoute) et ne vérifie aucun chart.
- **Au jalon 2.** Le verdict dépend des valeurs passées à Helm (`values.yaml` contre `values-prod.yaml`). L'étage `k8s-schema` rend une seule combinaison, ce qui peut faire passer à tort une règle sur l'image ou sur les ressources.
- **Vérification.** Sur deux ou trois dépôts réels de l'organisation, mesurer la part des ressources déployées qui viennent de fichiers bruts face à Helm et Kustomize. Comparer les violations sur une base et sur son overlay rendu.

**6. Le fonctionnement par type de politique est incertain et la fiabilité de la sortie n'est pas vérifiée.**
- **Les types de politiques.**
  - `generate` et `mutate` ne produisent pas de rapport de politiques. C'est attendu, mais c'est un silence que l'utilisateur prendra pour un « conforme ».
  - `verifyImages`, comme `ImageValidationPolicy`, demande l'accès au registre (`--registry`) : la vérification ne peut pas se faire sans réseau, et cosign est déjà intégré par ailleurs (`ToolCosign`).
  - La CLI applique `ValidatingPolicy` (CEL) et `ValidatingAdmissionPolicy`, mais avec des drapeaux et des fichiers de contexte différents.
- **Les règles générées automatiquement.** Kyverno réécrit une règle écrite sur `Pod` pour les contrôleurs (Deployment, CronJob…). Le rapport peut alors citer la règle `autogen-…` et non celle que l'utilisateur a écrite.
- **Les CRD inconnues.** Une ressource personnalisée sans schéma peut passer en silence ou être rejetée selon la version.
- **Les sorties de la CLI.** Le code de sortie 1 recouvre « violations » et « erreur », comme pour kubeconform. Une politique invalide dans le répertoire peut faire échouer tout l'étage. Le format JSON du rapport change selon les versions (1.4 à 1.19 diffèrent).
- **Vérification.** Un répertoire de test contenant une politique de chaque type (validate, CEL, generate, mutate, verifyImages, avec et sans autogen) plus une politique invalide. Relever pour chacun le code de sortie, stdout et stderr sur deux versions de la CLI.

**7. La maintenance dépend d'un tiers qui évolue vite.**
- **Pourquoi c'est un risque.** Kyverno remplace progressivement ClusterPolicy par les politiques CEL. Les flags de la CLI changent, l'image `ghcr.io/kyverno/kyverno-cli` est lourde, et le mode `image` impose de monter le répertoire de politiques en plus du dépôt scanné.
- **Conséquence.** L'organisation impose sa version de Kyverno ; si la CLI de DevDesk n'est pas alignée, elle juge différemment de ce que voit le cluster.
- **Vérification.** Lire le changelog de la CLI sur les quatre dernières versions mineures, en particulier les changements du format de rapport et des flags.

## Les 3 hypothèses à tester d'abord

1. **Les utilisateurs ciblés ont un jeu de politiques Kyverno accessible en local, que la CI ou l'admission ne les obligent pas déjà à respecter assez tôt.** À vérifier par entretiens, sinon la fonction n'a pas de demande.
2. **Une majorité des politiques réelles donne un verdict fiable hors cluster, sans contexte, sans `request.*` et sans registre.** À vérifier par un `apply` sur le vrai jeu, avec le classement pass, fail, skip ou error par politique.
3. **Une violation se rattache sans ambiguïté à un fichier et à une ligne, sur des dépôts structurés en base et overlays ou en charts.** C'est le critère qui a écarté kube-linter en §3.80. À mesurer sur deux ou trois dépôts réels avant tout cadrage.

Sources :
- [Kyverno CLI — apply (1.15)](https://release-1-15-0.kyverno.io/docs/kyverno-cli/usage/apply/)
- [Référence de kyverno apply (1.15)](https://release-1-15-0.kyverno.io/docs/kyverno-cli/reference/kyverno_apply/)
- [Kyverno CLI — test (1.15)](https://release-1-15-0.kyverno.io/docs/kyverno-cli/usage/test/)
- [kyverno.io — apply](https://kyverno.io/docs/kyverno-cli/usage/apply)
- [Kyverno CLI (1.4.3)](https://release-1-4-3.kyverno.io/docs/kyverno-cli)
